Claim_Current_Wording: Short-term supplements should be evaluated on operational outcomes rather than biomarker surrogates.
Evidence_Result: 12 mg/day astaxanthin for four weeks produced no statistically or clinically significant cardiometabolic or fire-ground performance effect; most inflammatory changes were within treatment groups.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that astaxanthin improves occupational performance or cardiometabolic health in firefighters or Brazilian public safety.

Claim_Current_Wording: Military supplementation effects are heterogeneous and require outcome-specific appraisal.
Evidence_Result: Sixteen studies reported inconsistent and mostly modest performance/recovery findings; authors state there is inadequate practical evidence for field performance guidance.
Relevant_Location: Methods 2; Results 3 and Table 3; Limitations 4.4; Conclusions 5.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not justify a general supplementation protocol, causal field-readiness claim, or direct transfer to Brazilian public safety.

Claim_Current_Wording: In a small firefighter trial, creatine added to protein/carbohydrate was associated with improvement in selected task times.
Evidence_Result: Creatine group showed larger improvement in rescue (difference 1.78 s, 95% CI 0.61-2.95; p=.004) and forcible entry (2.66 s, 95% CI 0.68-4.65; p=.01), with no interaction for other tasks or total time.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show that protein/carbohydrate alone caused benefit, that every occupational task improved, or that results generalize to female firefighters or Brazilian agencies.

Claim_Current_Wording: The 30-15 IFT showed reproducible cardiorespiratory-fitness estimates in one infantry cohort.
Evidence_Result: End-running speed, maximal heart rate and predicted VO2max test-retest ICCs were .971, .960 and .975; authors report validity/usefulness against treadmill and 2-mile run measures.
Relevant_Location: Methods: Study design and procedures; Results and Table 2; Conclusion.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not validate the test for Brazilian policing, establish combat readiness, or prove outcome prediction beyond this small infantry cohort.

Claim_Current_Wording: Body armour can increase workload and impair selected physical-task outcomes; effects are outcome- and system-specific.
Evidence_Result: Across 16 eligible studies, authors report increased workload, lower work capacity, slower functional-task completion, impaired balance/stability and higher RPE; marksmanship and some physiological effects remain uncertain.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not quantify the effect of a particular Brazilian vest, prove injury prevention effects, or establish cognitive/marksmanship decrement in all settings.

Claim_Current_Wording: Automated positive feedback may improve selected implementation perceptions within a specific policing deployment.
Evidence_Result: In two Arizona departments (n=84 responses), adjusted probability of rating the platform appropriate was 21.7 percentage points higher in the feedback department (p=.011); feasibility was not significant.
Relevant_Location: Pilot 03: Setting; Tables 1-4; Limitations; Conclusion. FT1 digest: Methods, Results, Discussion and Conclusion.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish improved officer behavior, public safety, accountability, technology accuracy, causal organization-wide benefit or Brazilian applicability.

Claim_Current_Wording: Selected US police leaders reported CFIR-aligned barriers and facilitators relevant to planning, not effectiveness.
Evidence_Result: Seventy-two respondents, mostly senior personnel, described innovation complexity, limited tailoring and low trust of external implementers; data are descriptive and convenience-sampled.
Relevant_Location: Pilot 03: Study population; Survey measures; Results/Table 3-5; Limitations. FT1 digest confirms Methods, Results and Conclusion.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish prevalence across US policing, causal determinants of implementation success, innovation effectiveness or transferability to Brazil.

Claim_Current_Wording: Hydration monitoring proposals for firefighters require direct outcome evaluation before institutional adoption.
Evidence_Result: Review recommends multi-measure hydration assessment and notes no firefighter randomized trials demonstrating health effects of maintained euhydration.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that the suggested volumes or thresholds improve health, performance or safety in firefighters or Brazilian public safety.
